name: publr.plugin.define(manifest, options)
summary: The one registration Publr looks for in main.zig: everything the plugin adds, as options. A misspelt option fails the build.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins.
On the sampler site it is under Built-in.
look_for: sampler listed, enabled, version 0.1.0.

options.name: .register_fields
options.summary: A typed field group on users, media or any type, placed by .location.
see: Open Settings, then Users, then Admin.
options.look_for: A Sampler profile group with a Motto field.

tour.say: Open an account.
The sampler's field group, with its Motto field.

options.name: .register_statuses
options.summary: Adds a status and its transitions to another plugin's flow: Sampled on greeter's salutations.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
options.look_for: Add the status Sampled to greeter.salutation; records go in and out by Sample it and Release.

tour.find: Records go in and out by
tour.say: The status the sampler adds to greeter's salutations, one of its requests on its page.

options.name: .row_actions
options.summary: An action on the rows of a page that names a slot: here, any page naming the sampler slot.
see: No page names the sampler slot yet; the action is read by a page's owner.
options.look_for: Open the log, offered to whoever may read the logs.

options.name: .routes, .settings_pages (compiled in only)
options.summary: Routes of the plugin's own and a Settings page listing them: compiled in only, left out of the installed build.
see: On the sampler site, open Settings.
Under Plugins, open Sampler.
options.look_for: The log and the port serve noted, drawn by the plugin's own route.

options.name: .State, .serving, .before_command, .operator_commands (compiled in only)
options.summary: Process-wide state and hooks on the process itself: compiled in only.
see: POST /_publr/sampler/ping with the operator key.
options.look_for: The port serve noted, and how many pings.

tour.say: The sampler, listed among the plugins with its description and version.

name: publr.Manifest
summary: The plugin's name and version. Its description is the top //! comment of main.zig: the first line in lists, the rest on its page.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
look_for: Its name, the first line of main.zig's //! comment under it, Version 0.1.0; the rest of the comment further down, under From sampler.

tour.find: A sample of every part of the plugin contract, for the two-mode check.
tour.say: The first line of main.zig's //! comment is the description; the version sits beside it.

name: publr.MenuItem
summary: A menu item of the plugin's own in the admin's sidebar. Its records and other plugins attach to it by name, sampler.notes.
see: Open Content from the rail.
Look at its sidebar.
look_for: A Sample notes heading with the sampler's note icon, the sampler's types under it.

options.name: .icon, with .icons
options.summary: The icon an item draws: one of the set, or one of the plugin's own, declared in define's .icons and named <plugin>.<name>; every drawing goes through the SVG sanitizer.
see: Open Content from the rail.
Look at its sidebar.
options.look_for: The Sample notes heading draws sampler.note: a note with a folded corner.

tour.say: sampler.note, the plugin's own icon, drawn beside the heading.
The sampler's menu item: a heading in Content's sidebar, its types under it.

name: publr.operation.define(In, Out, options)
summary: An input type, an output type and a function. Its words are the file's //! comment: the description, the details and an Example the build checks.
see: In the site's folder, run: publr sampler hello --help
Then: publr sampler hello --who you
look_for: The help shows the description and each field's words; the answer is { "text": "hello, you" }.

options.name: .untrusted_callers
options.summary: Anyone may call the operation, a site's pages too, at /_actions/app.sampler.<verb>. Without .authorize, anyone at all.
see: In the site's folder, run publr sampler hello without --as.
options.look_for: It answers without anyone signed in.

options.name: .authorize
options.summary: A ready answer to who may call: anyone signed in. It needs .untrusted_callers.
see: Run publr sampler wave --who Ada without --as.
Then with --as-admin, then with --as admin@publr.localhost.
options.look_for: Refused for nobody; Hi for the administrator on the command line, let through but not signed in; Hi, Ada for someone signed in.

options.name: .validate, publr.Problems
options.summary: Checks what belongs to the call, every problem at once, each beside its field. Its /// is the Checked line in --help.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler wave --who "".
options.look_for: Refused as invalid input, the problem under --who: A name is 1 to 40 characters.

options.name: .limit
options.summary: A stricter rate limit for untrusted callers: a site's pages and anyone without credentials.
see: Call /_actions/app.sampler.wave from a page more than 30 times in a minute.
options.look_for: 429 Too Many Requests, with the RateLimit headers.

name: publr.Ctx
summary: What an operation's or a hook's code reaches Publr through: the call's memory and time, who is calling, other operations, events and queued work.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler note --note hello.
look_for: note comes back in capitals with the number of notes kept.

options.name: ctx.print(fmt, args)
options.summary: Formatted text in memory that lives until the call ends.
see: Run publr --as admin@publr.localhost sampler wave --who Ada.
options.look_for: Hi, Ada.

options.name: ctx.alloc(T, n)
options.summary: Memory for the call, failing with publr.Error rather than a raw allocator error.
see: Open the Sampler log page after adding a note.
options.look_for: The note is logged in capitals: the before hook made them in memory from ctx.alloc.

options.name: ctx.caller()
options.summary: Who is calling: whether signed in, their roles, the visitor's id, where the call came from.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler wave --who Ada, then publr --as admin@publr.localhost sampler wave --who Ada.
options.look_for: Hi without --as's person, Hi, Ada with them: the run asks whether someone is signed in.

options.name: ctx.call(Operation, in)
options.summary: Any operation, core's under publr.operations, through the same checks as every caller.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler note --note hello.
options.look_for: total counts every sample note: core's record.List, called as the sampler.

options.name: ctx.mod(name, value)
options.summary: Applies a value under a name and answers it as every modifier left it. The sampler doubles every number it applies, through * for one dotted part.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
Then run publr --as-admin sampler measure --text abc.
options.look_for: Change sampler.* wherever it is used, because it: Doubles every number sampler applies. length comes back as 6.

options.name: ctx.emit(Event, payload)
options.summary: Emits an event of the plugin's own: after hooks hear it in the write, on hooks from the queue once it commits.
see: Add a note, then open the Sampler log page.
options.look_for: A new line, noted <NOTE>: the event reached the on hook.

options.name: ctx.enqueue(Job, in)
options.summary: Queues a job, written in the same transaction; the queue worker runs it after the call.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler later --note Remember.
Open the sample reviews list.
options.look_for: A draft review Remember, written by the job a moment later.

tour.say: The draft review the job wrote, from the queue.

options.name: ctx.now(), publr.Time
options.summary: The call's time, one value for the whole call or job run, the type datetime fields hold.
see: Run publr --as-admin job list.
options.look_for: tick waiting, due at 03:00.

name: publr.text
summary: The text helpers plugins need every day, named as JavaScript's String names them, so no plugin writes std.mem.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler submit --text spam.
look_for: Refused: A review says something of its own.

options.name: equals(a, b)
options.summary: The same text, byte for byte.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler submit --text spam.
options.look_for: Refused: A review says something of its own.

name: publr.record.define(T, options)
summary: A content type from a struct: its fields from the struct and their ///, the title, the menu it sits under, the columns its list shows.
see: Open Content from the rail.
In its sidebar, under Sample notes, open Sample note.
look_for: The notes listed by their titles, the Note column beside them.

options.name: .fields: .validation
options.summary: A field's rules, checked on every write whoever writes, written out beside the field's help.
see: Open a sample note and empty its Note field.
Save.
options.look_for: The save is refused with the problem under Note.

options.name: .internal, .indexed, .append_only
options.summary: Bookkeeping never shown in Content: looked up by an indexed field, written once and never changed.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
Scroll to Its data.
options.look_for: tally, Internal records, one per note kept: core knows the plugin's bookkeeping, never shown in Content.

tour.say: The tallies, the plugin's bookkeeping, counted under Its data; never in Content.

options.name: .status, publr.record.Transition(Status)
options.summary: The statuses a record can be in and the transitions between them; any other is refused. A transition may say who may run it.
see: Open Content, then Sample review.
Open the draft Remember the milk.
options.look_for: Submit for review where a draft of core's flow says Publish. Once in review the editor offers Publish: it does not show the flow's Approve label yet.

tour.say: Open a draft review.
The flow's own transition, where core's flow says Publish.

options.name: .validate
options.summary: A record checks its own data on every create and save, whoever writes.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler submit --text spam.
options.look_for: Refused as invalid input, the problem under --text: A review says something of its own. The record's own check, run on create.

options.name: The handle: create, get, transition
options.summary: A record's handle: create starts at .start, transition names a transition of the flow and answers .done or .pending.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler submit --text "Looks good".
options.look_for: status is in_review.

tour.say: The sample notes, listed by title with their Note column.

name: publr.records.of, publr.internal.of
summary: A plugin's records as typed values, created and found by field.
see: Look at the top bar's right end.
look_for: Sampler log with the number of notes beside it.

name: publr.event.define(options)
summary: An event of the plugin's own, a payload with /// on each field, listed in .events and emitted with ctx.emit.
see: Add a note, then open the Sampler log page.
look_for: noted <NOTE>: the line the event's on hook wrote.

name: publr.before(Target, run)
summary: Inside the write, before the operation: may change its input or refuse. Its /// is the reason the administrator reads.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
Then run publr --as-admin sampler note --note hello.
look_for: Change what is sent to the sampler.note operation, because it: Keeps every note in capitals. The note comes back as HELLO.

name: publr.after(Target, run)
summary: Inside the write, after the operation: gets its input and answer, may refuse, which rolls the write back.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
look_for: See when the sampler.note operation happens, because it: Tells other plugins a note was kept.

name: publr.on(Target, run)
summary: From the queue, once the write committed; never in the caller's request. May call other servers.
see: Open Settings, then Sampler log.
look_for: A line per note kept, each written by this hook from the queue.

tour.say: Each line here was written by the on hook, from the queue.

name: publr.modify(name, run)
summary: Changes a value wherever its owner applies it, the way WordPress's add_filter does; * stands for one dotted part. Its /// is the reason the administrator reads.
see: Open Content, then Sample note under Sample notes.
look_for: Each title reads Note: <note> (<n> characters): the modifier, applied wherever the title shows.

options.name: "<type>.title", publr.Title
options.summary: Changes a value wherever its owner applies it; core applies each record's title as <type>.title.
see: Open Content, then Sample note under Sample notes.
options.look_for: Each title reads Note: <note> (<n> characters): the modifier, applied wherever the title shows.

tour.say: The title as the modifier left it: Note: <note> (<n> characters).

options.name: "sampler.*", with ctx.mod
options.summary: Applies a value under a name and answers it as every modifier left it. The sampler doubles every number it applies, through * for one dotted part.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
Then run publr --as-admin sampler measure --text abc.
options.look_for: Change sampler.* wherever it is used, because it: Doubles every number sampler applies. length comes back as 6.

tour.say: The title as the modifier left it: Note: <note> (<n> characters).

name: publr.job.define(In, options)
summary: The plugin's own queued work, listed in .jobs, queued with ctx.enqueue, retried with growing waits.
see: Run publr --as-admin sampler later --note Remember.
Open Content, then Sample review.
look_for: A new draft review, Remember, written by the job a moment later. publr --as-admin job list shows runs only while they wait or after they failed.

options.name: publr.job.define_recurring(options)
options.summary: Work that repeats: .every a day, an hour or minutes, .at a time in UTC.
see: Run publr --as-admin job list.
options.look_for: sampler tick waiting, due at the next 03:00 UTC.

options.name: .due, a record's datetime field
options.summary: Work that follows a content record's datetime field: queued by every write to the record, run before or after the field's moment, given the record as it is then.
see: Open Content, then Sample note, and set a note's Remind me at to an hour from now.
Run publr --as-admin job list.
options.look_for: sampler remind waiting, due half an hour before the note's reminder time.

tour.say: The review the job wrote.

name: publr.webhook.define(Event, options)
summary: What another server sends to /_webhooks/<plugin>.<name>: the signature checked with a declared secret, 200 answered at once, run as queued work with the body as Event; a repeat dropped.
see: Set SAMPLER_KEY under Settings, then Secrets.
Send POST /_webhooks/sampler.ping with X-Sampler-Key set to it and the body {"id":"1","text":"Hello"}.
Open Plugins, then sampler, then Webhooks.
look_for: The delivery, verified and ran, with the line webhook ping: Hello.

name: publr.Page
summary: A page of the plugin's own under Settings, drawn by a read of its own, the same built in and installed.
see: Open Settings, then Sampler log.
look_for: The log in the admin's own table, inside the plugin's frame.

options.name: .top_bar = .{ .count }
options.summary: The page in the top bar too, a read's count beside its label.
see: Open any admin page.
Look at the top bar's right end.
options.look_for: Sampler log, with the number of notes.

tour.say: The page in the top bar, the notes counted beside it.
The sampler's page, drawn by its read in the plugin frame.

name: publr.views.render(ctx, base, View, props)
summary: A page from the plugin's own PTSX view. Installed, the host draws every design-system component it reaches, so the page reads like a compiled-in one.
see: Open Settings, then Sampler log, on both sampler and sampler-sandboxed.
look_for: The same page both ways.

tour.say: The sampler's page, drawn by its read in the plugin frame.

name: publr.Panel
summary: A box on another type's edit form, drawn by a read of the plugin's own in the plugin frame, told only the record's id.
see: Open Content, then Sample note under Sample notes.
Open Note: HELLO.
look_for: A Sampler box beside the form: Note <id>, one of <n>.

tour.say: Open a note.
The Sampler box, drawn by the sampler's read in the plugin frame.

name: publr.Secret
summary: The secrets a plugin declares; it never holds the value. {secret:NAME} is filled as a fetch leaves.
see: Open Settings, then Secrets.
look_for: SAMPLER_KEY, used by sampler, Missing until someone sets its value.

tour.say: The key the sampler declares, used by sampler, Missing until it is set.

name: publr.Permission
summary: What the plugin asks the administrator for, each with its reason; outside calls only to the domains named.
see: On sampler-sandboxed, open Settings, then Plugins, then sampler.
look_for: Send requests to the domains it names, sampler.example in its Domains box, the Sampler key under it, High risk.

tour.find: Send requests to the domains it names
tour.say: What the sampler asks for: http.fetch to sampler.example, with its reason.
